brief: The Fed hiked 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%, its first hike since 2023, in a unanimous 12-0 vote. Chair Warsh's hawkish press conference cited a resilient economy and persistent inflation as reasons to act now toward the 2% target. The dot plot shows one more hike by year-end then no change through 2027, which the note reads as a mid-cycle adjustment rather than a prolonged tightening cycle, so the hike should not change the growth or earnings outlook. Market reaction: 2-year yield to 4.73% (two-year high), 10-year back above 5%, S&P 500 -0.4%, dollar +0.6%, oil down nearly 3%. Separately, SPR releases slowed to ~400k barrels last week as reserves near minimum safety levels; US output rebounded to a record ~14m bpd, but that only offsets ~5% of the Persian Gulf shortfall, so the deficit needs demand destruction until the Strait of Hormuz reopens. The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index and the 10-year yield now show the most negative 90-day correlation since 1996, a reversal from growth-signal to financing-headwind, a near-term equity challenge until yields ease. August retail sales rose 1.2% MoM, with the control group (+1.4%) pointing to a 3Q GDP boost, though the note expects spending to moderate from that pace.
